summary.title: Cycle Time
summary.one_liner: Cycle time, the speed at which decisions and iterations move through an organization, is driven mainly by how many vertical escalation levels and how many people are involved, so decision-making should be pushed down and meetings and documents kept small.
keywords: how to speed up decisions at scale
takeaways: Cycle time is a function of how many vertical levels a discussion traverses and how many people are involved at each level.
Push decision making down to senior individual contributors and strong local leaders instead of defaulting to org-chart ownership.
Escalate early and often, and assign a Single Threaded Owner who is fully focused on each critical area of work.
Keep documents and meetings small; representation of each discipline need not mean direct attendance.
Make decisions durable using demos and prototypes, reduce unnecessary parallel work, and keep processes updated.
summary.summary: This short essay argues that organizational structure and process determine cycle time, which in turn affects execution speed and team satisfaction. The author explains that cycle time depends on the number of vertical escalation levels and the number of people involved at each level, and lists ways to reduce it: pushing decisions down, escalating early, using single-threaded owners, shrinking documents and meetings through representation, making decisions durable with prototypes, doing less, removing bottlenecks, and keeping processes well maintained. It is a reflective opinion piece rather than a tutorial, with no code or data.
